headline: Single-cell and spatial profiles resolve tumor and tissue immune niches across organs
label: Single Cell And Spatial Transcriptomics
summary: Spatially resolved and single-cell profiling now links specific immune cell states to niche architecture and checkpoint therapy response.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to place immune and stromal cell states within their tissue niches. Several studies tie specific T cell or macrophage states to immunotherapy outcome: TSTScope integrates scRNA-seq with TCR sequencing to identify predictive tumor-specific T cell states, gastric cancer work links CD8+ T cell heterogeneity to checkpoint response, and kidney cancer persister cells revert to embryonic nephrogenic programs under blockade. Spatial studies add locational context, including ectopic GC-like niches in lung adenocarcinoma, GZMB+ cytotoxic lymphocytes constrained by cell death-associated niches in glioblastoma, and altered macrophage states in skin cancer. The most distinctive methodological advance is Stereo-XCR-seq, which recovers TCR and BCR sequences from spatial transcriptome cDNA libraries at subcellular resolution. Other items extend the framework to macrophage checkpoint regulation, thymic selection during aging, and circulating B cell heterogeneity.
